title: OpenMobile-2 trains phone agents on more than 110 resettable apps
friendlyTitle: An open project trains phone agents on more than 110 apps you can reset
summary: Researchers from Nanjing University, SenseTime, and other labs have released OpenMobile-2, with open training environments and recipes for mobile agents. MobileGym++ rebuilds 35 commercial-style apps so a run can be reset and checked, and with emulator apps the playground covers more than 110. They release about 12,000 supervised trajectories and more than 2,000 tasks with automatic rewards. The larger model scores 79.9 on AndroidWorld and 50.4 on MobileWorld. On real Android phones, SPA-Bench rises from 31.9 to 59.6.
friendlySummary: Researchers have released OpenMobile-2, with the practice environments and the training recipe for agents that use a phone. They rebuilt 35 commercial-style apps so a practice run can be reset and checked. With emulator apps, the playground covers more than 110. They also release about 12,000 example sessions and more than 2,000 tasks with an automatic pass or fail. The larger model scores 79.9 on AndroidWorld and 50.4 on MobileWorld. On real Android phones, a benchmark called SPA-Bench rises from 31.9 to 59.6.
whyItMatters: A phone agent you cannot reset is a demo. This one publishes the practice ground, the tasks, and the check for whether the task actually finished. The real-phone jump is the number that matters if you want an agent on a handset rather than in a simulator. An experimental mode also lets some simulated apps expose a direct command, such as add-to-cart, beside ordinary taps. That part exists in the simulation, not yet as a switch on the phone in your pocket.
